reader_summary.headline: How do you build, set, shape, fix, and change your culture?
reader_summary.overview: How do you build, set, shape, fix, and change your culture? While this is as relevant as ever for startups and companies today, leaders have sought the answers to these questions for hundreds of years. In this episode from December 2019, A16Z co-founder Ben Horowitz sits down with host Sonal Choxy to talk about what actually makes up culture.

positions.commentary: Reed Hastings is described as a first principles thinker who successfully pivoted Netflix from DVD to streaming by prioritizing the vision of a network over the immediate revenue of the DVD business.
Travis Kalanick failed to define ethical lines at Uber, allowing a competitive culture to be interpreted as 'whatever at all cost', which resulted in sexual harassment of employees.

thesis: This episode argues that successful companies like Netflix succeed because leaders prioritize long-term vision and first principles over immediate revenue, whereas companies like Uber fail when competitive cultures lack defined ethical boundaries, leading to severe reputational and operational damage.
